CTDL1901.d: This course provides an introduction to critical thinking and data literacy. Students will be equipped with critical tools to analyse problems of reasoning, evaluate the truthfulness of evidence, examine the fallacies of thinking, as well as the ability to construct valid arguments and reasonable solutions for their personal and professional life.
cl: Identify and analyze relevant information, data, and sources for problems
Construct valid arguments using analytical skills, data, and evidence
Justify solutions with relevant criteria and standards
Evaluate implications and consequences of the solutions
Communicate decisions effectively using data and evidence

CTDL1902.d: This course explores how artificial intelligence (AI) will impact society and the economy. It covers key topics such as ethics, social justice, and the benefits and existential risks of AI. Throughout the course, students will learn about AI through by using AI to complete various tasks. The course is designed around active learning exercises encouraging students to develop hybrid critical thinking skills, which leverage generative AI to extend their natural human capabilities. Students will be expected to learn how to maximize the benefits gained from AI assistance while avoiding potential pitfalls. The course employs a range of assessment methods, including group projects and individual reflection journals, to foster both collaborative learning and personal growth.
cl: Explain the fundamental concepts of AI, its capabilities and limitations, and its potential impact on the society and economy
Explain how AI differs from human cognition, and how AI may complement and/or disrupt human cognition
Apply critical thinking skills to evaluate AI technologies, particularly in the context of cognitive science theories and human-machine relationships
Analyze the role of AI in society using network theory, complexity theory, ethical theories, and other relevant theoretical frameworks
Demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively about AI, its role in society, and its social, economic, and ethical implications

CTDL1950.d: In today’s fast-paced world, strong thinking skills are essential for academic success and personal growth across various disciplines. This interdisciplinary course, offered by Academy of Interdisciplinary Studies, is designed for junior-level students to enhance their critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities by integrating perspectives from multiple fields. Through engaging in interactive activities and discussions, students will learn to analyze information, evaluate arguments, and develop creative solutions to real-world challenges that span different domains. These skills are not only vital for effective learning but also prepare students for future careers and responsible citizenship. By fostering a mindset of inquiry and reflection, this course empowers students to become confident thinkers and informed decision-makers in an ever-changing environment.
cl: Address issues with a systems thinking mindset
Apply design thinking tools to understand users’ needs and identify a problem statement
Describe the different types and attributes of data, assess the data quality and select  the appropriate data collection method
Apply the analytics framework for problem analysis and decision making
Communicate and persuade the audience through a structured approach to report the problem and solutions of the issue
